clue.text: Heading from bar, say, with measures of alcohol for one who spills a lot

parts.note: one who butts strikes with the head, as a player heading the ball off the crossbar does, so such a striker is a butter
a finger is a measure of spirits poured to the depth of a finger's width in the glass

explanation.surface: A drinker knocking back measures at the bar earns a reputation for clumsiness with glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, sitting beside 'alcohol', but here it is the goal's crossbar off which a ball is headed; 'with' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clumsy who keeps dropping and spilling things is mocked with this word for slippery hands.

clue.text: Getting on coach for Winchester, perhaps

parts.note: boarding means getting on a vehicle
to coach is to train or school someone

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard a bus bound for the city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting on and coach suggest a bus trip to Winchester; coach is a verb meaning train. Winchester College is an old English private school where pupils live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchester College is a famous English school where pupils live on site, an example of the type.

clue.text: Helpful hint about extremely unusual bulb

indicators.note: about means around, so the hint goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A gardening tip about a very unusual bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip grows from a bulb, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Natural way to achieve financial security

parts.note: easy means relaxed and natural, as in an easy manner
a street is a way or road

explanation.surface: Advice on the natural route to becoming financially secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this proverbial road is an idiom for living in comfort with plenty of money.

clue.text: Hang the Spanish workers' offshore accommodation!

parts.note: to hang in the air or water is to float
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about the oil workers' floating hostel.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating hotel housing workers on oil and gas rigs out at sea goes by this blended name.

clue.text: A number going round and calling in maze

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the number is read backwards

parts.note: ten is a number
a calling is one's job or work

explanation.surface: A figure turns round while calling out inside a maze.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is an intricate system of crossing paths, which a maze is too.

clue.text: Contest not finished yet

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter is missing

parts.note: an event is a contest in a sports meeting

explanation.surface: A report that the match has not yet finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words intensify a comparison, as in yet more or even more, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Foremost of surgeons, decorated, began to operate

indicators.note: foremost of takes only the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: tarted up means decorated, often showily

explanation.surface: The leading surgeons, dressed up in finery, have begun to operate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operate' suggests surgery; here it means a machine or business starting to run.
explanation.definitionFit: When an engine or business started running it began operating, so the phrasal verb fits.

clue.text: Waste one's time, and forge a shedload inaccurately

indicators.note: done inaccurately, the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wasting time and churning out masses of sloppy forgeries.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means persisting with effort on something already settled or hopeless, wasting one's time.

clue.text: Book finally reduced

indicators.note: reduced tells us to cut the phrase short, losing its last letter

parts.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: A terse note that a book has at last been marked down in price.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound collection of maps is a kind of book.

clue.text: Informed about article to appear before social function

parts.note: about means on, as in a talk on a subject
the is the definite article
a ball is a formal dance, a social function

explanation.surface: A society reporter learns what will appear at an upcoming party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and well informed is an idiom describing someone who is quick on the uptake.

clue.text: Evidence of French state of affairs

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a position is a situation or state of affairs

explanation.surface: A note that a French state of affairs counts as proof.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn statement taken out of court is used as evidence at trial.

clue.text: Male part shortened

indicators.note: shortened tells us to cut the last letter off the word for part

parts.note: a stage is a part or leg of a journey

explanation.surface: A male role in a play has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male' looks like an adjective describing the part, but it is the definition, a noun for a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown male deer is called by this name, so it stands for a male animal.

clue.text: Reportedly tracks down account in plant

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word that sounds like the next one is used

parts.note: stalks means follows and tracks down
a bill is an account of money owed

explanation.surface: Reports say someone has tracked down an account hidden in a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Storksbill is a wild flower of the geranium family, named for its beaked fruit.

clue.text: Figure manure must be spread, then left

indicators.note: spreading muck scatters it about, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction: the muck must be spread, then the ground left alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a symbol representing a number, which is what a figure is.

clue.text: Primate's prize tree

parts.note: a monkey is a primate
a pot is a prize or trophy, a cup

explanation.surface: A tree is the prize an ape has won.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey pot is a South American tree whose lidded fruits are pot-shaped.

clue.text: Coolidge's girl carried out an insect

parts.note: Katy is the heroine of What Katy Did, the children's novel by Susan Coolidge
carried out means did, as of a task

explanation.surface: A girl surnamed Coolidge has carried an insect outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Coolidge suggests the US president, but it is Susan Coolidge, author of What Katy Did; the clue nods to that title.
explanation.definitionFit: A katydid is a North American bush cricket, named after its call, so it is an insect.

clue.text: Italian resort in Ransome novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the author's name is made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An Italian holiday town appears in a book by Arthur Ransome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a noun, a Ransome book, but it is an adjective meaning new, the anagram signal. Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: San Remo is a seaside resort on the Italian Riviera in Liguria.

clue.text: Exaggerate about something done

parts.note: over means about, as in a dispute over money
an act is a deed, something done

explanation.surface: Making a fuss about something that has already been done.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to exaggerate one's performance on stage.

clue.text: Roman general, an old man seizing control

indicators.note: seizing means taking hold of, so the word for control is held inside the other letters

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
grip means control, as in a firm grip on things

explanation.surface: A Roman general is pictured as an old man grabbing power.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman general who won the battle of Actium for Octavian.

clue.text: A grant secured by the gymnast, maybe

indicators.note: secured by means held within, so the word for grant sits inside the article

parts.note: to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: A grant has been won by the gymnast.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast is one example of a sports competitor, hence maybe.

clue.text: Last of such fish in list

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A request to list the last of such fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a noun meaning a catalogue, but it is a verb: a ship that lists leans over to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans to one side is said to keel over or tilt, and both verbs share that sense.

clue.text: Old man with a lot of bottle

definitions.meaning: the patriarch of Genesis said to have lived 969 years, the oldest man in the Bible
a very large wine bottle holding eight standard bottles

explanation.surface: An old fellow with plenty of nerve, bottle being slang for courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' tempts as British slang for courage; here it means a literal wine bottle of great size.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share a name: the biblical patriarch famed for longevity, and a giant champagne bottle named after him.

clue.text: Crease? Any number in this cloth

parts.note: a line is a crease or wrinkle
n stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Ironing a crease out of some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a fabric woven from flax, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Reverse taxi over top of kerb

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the vehicle is read backwards in a down clue

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter, the top in a down clue

explanation.surface: A driver reverses the cab up onto the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse a vehicle is to drive it backwards, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: One could look after the children if their parents are late

definitions.text: One could look after the children if their parents are late

parts.words: One could look after the children if their parents are late
parts.note: late here means dead, not delayed: an institution that cares for children whose parents have died

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' suggests parents delayed at work and a babysitter; it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a home for children whose parents have died, so it cares for them.

clue.text: Private meal daughter fails to attend

indicators.note: fails to attend means is absent, so the letter is removed

parts.note: dinner is the main meal of the day

explanation.surface: A private family meal goes ahead though the daughter does not turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, kept within, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: The confirmed bachelor won't do something decisive

definitions.meaning: what a man set against marriage refuses to do: get married
commit boldly to a course of action

explanation.surface: A determined single man refuses to make a bold commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to marry and, more generally, to commit to a bold step.
